# Introduction to forecasting

## What is a forecast?

Estimating how a sequence of observations will continue into the future, using all information available now.

```{r}
#| label: beer-forecast
#| include: false
beer <- tail(ausbeer, 60)
beer_fit <- ausbeer |> model(ETS(Production))
set.seed(2026)
beer_paths <- beer_fit |> generate(h = 20, times = 30)
beer_fc <- beer_fit |>
  forecast(h = 20) |>
  mutate(`80%` = hilo(Production, 80), `95%` = hilo(Production, 95)) |>
  unpack_hilo(c(`80%`, `95%`))

# Each frame shares its scales, so the frames line up when stacked
beer_plot <- function(paths = 0, intervals = FALSE) {
  p <- ggplot(beer, aes(x = Time, y = Production)) +
    geom_line() +
    expand_limits(
      x = range(beer_paths$Time),
      y = range(beer_paths$.sim, beer_fc$`95%_lower`, beer_fc$`95%_upper`)
    ) +
    labs(x = "Quarter", y = "Megalitres", title = "Quarterly Australian beer production")
  if (paths > 0) {
    p <- p + geom_line(
      aes(y = .sim, group = .rep),
      data = filter(beer_paths, as.integer(.rep) <= paths),
      colour = "#3B75AC", alpha = if (paths == 1) 1 else 0.4
    )
  }
  if (intervals) {
    p <- p +
      geom_ribbon(aes(y = NULL, ymin = `95%_lower`, ymax = `95%_upper`),
                  data = beer_fc, fill = "#3B75AC", alpha = 0.25) +
      geom_ribbon(aes(y = NULL, ymin = `80%_lower`, ymax = `80%_upper`),
                  data = beer_fc, fill = "#3B75AC", alpha = 0.35) +
      geom_line(aes(y = .mean), data = beer_fc, colour = "#3B75AC")
  }
  p
}
```

<!-- One frame visible at a time: the transparent plots would double their gridlines if stacked -->
::: {.r-stack}
::: {.fragment .fade-out fragment-index=1}
```{r beer-data, echo=FALSE, dependson="beer-forecast"}
beer_plot()
```
:::

::: {.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=1}

:::

::: {.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=2}

:::

::: {.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=3}

## What data do we need?

1. Historical data on the variable to forecast
2. Past and future values of predictors
    + Deterministic (e.g. holidays)
    + Stochastic (e.g. temperature)
3. Expert knowledge and context
    + New information

## Why forecast?

Why do you use forecasts?

::: {.fragment}
| Decision                                    | Forecast                                       |
| ------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| Build a new hospital in the next 10 years?  | [Population and patient demand, years ahead]{.fragment} |
| Call centre staff needed next week?         | [Call volumes, hours to days ahead]{.fragment}           |
| Vaccine doses needed next month?            | [Doses by region, weeks ahead]{.fragment}                |
:::

::: {.fragment}
::: {.block}
The decision sets [what]{.alert} to forecast and [how far ahead]{.alert}.
:::
:::

# Time series data

## Time series data

* Four-yearly Olympic winning times
* Annual Google profits
* Quarterly Australian beer production
* Monthly rainfall
* Weekly retail sales
* Daily IBM stock prices
* Hourly electricity demand
* 5-minute freeway traffic counts
* Time-stamped stock transaction data

## Your time series

::: {.wordcloud #your-time-series max-words=3 max-answers=3}
What time series data do you work with?
:::

## What makes it a time series?

::: {.block}
Observations + [when]{.alert} they happened.
:::

* The time column is the [index]{.alert}
* Observations are ordered in time
* Regular intervals define the frequency (yearly, quarterly, ...)

# tsibble objects

## A `tsibble` has three parts

::: {.block}
A [tsibble]{.alert} stores one or more time series in a table.
:::

* **Index**: when
* **Key**: which series (optional)
* **Measures**: what was observed

Works with dplyr verbs (`filter()`, `mutate()`, ...).

## `tsibble` objects

```{r, echo = TRUE}
global_economy
```

## The `tsibble` index

For annual data, integer years work as the index:

```{r tstable}
annual_data <- tsibble(
  year = 2012:2016,
  y = c(123, 39, 78, 52, 110),
  index = year
)
annual_data
```

## The `tsibble` index

```{r tstablemonth, echo=FALSE}
monthly_data <- tibble(Month = paste(2019, month.abb[1:5]), Observation = c(50, 23, 34, 30, 25))
```

```{r tstablemonth2}
monthly_data
```

::: {.fragment}
* `"2019 Jan"` is just text
* More frequent than yearly? Use a time class
:::

## The `tsibble` index

```{r month-tsibble}
monthly_data |>
  mutate(Month = yearmonth(Month)) |>
  as_tsibble(index = Month)
```

## The `tsibble` index

Common time index variables can be created with these functions:

```{r tstable2, echo=FALSE}
tribble(
  ~`Frequency`, ~Function,
  "Annual", "`start:end`",
  "Quarterly", "`yearquarter()`",
  "Monthly", "`yearmonth()`",
  "Weekly", "`yearweek()`",
  "Daily", "`as_date()`, `ymd()`",
  "Sub-daily", "`as_datetime()`, `ymd_hms()`"
) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

## Converting dates

Often data is provided as dates, even if it isn't daily.

```{r convert-dates}
my_date <- as.Date("2026-10-01")
yearquarter(my_date)
yearmonth(my_date)
yearweek(my_date)
```

## Looking ahead: `mixtime` {.code-small}

![](figs/mixtime.png){.absolute top="-36px" right="-50px" height="100px"}

One family of linear time classes, including `year()` and `datetime()`:

```{r mixtime-linear, cache=FALSE}
library(mixtime)
c(year(my_date), yearquarter(my_date), yearmonth(my_date), date(my_date))
```

::: {.fragment}
Any granularity: pick a [chronon]{.alert} (one time step) and call `linear_time()`:

```{r mixtime-chronon, cache=FALSE}
quarter_hours <- datetime("2024-01-01 00:00:00") + minutes(0:3) * 15L
linear_time(quarter_hours, chronon = cal_gregorian$minute(15L))
```

* `yearmonth(my_date)` is `linear_time(my_date, chronon = cal_gregorian$month(1L))`
:::

## Looking ahead: `mixtime` {.code-small}

![](figs/mixtime.png){.absolute top="-36px" right="-50px" height="100px"}

More time types, beyond this course:

```{r mixtime-more, cache=FALSE}
# Timezones
datetime(as.POSIXct("2026-10-05 22:30", tz = "UTC"), tz = "Africa/Nairobi")
# Other calendars (also cal_isoweek, lunar and solar calendars)
linear_time(my_date, chronon = cal_sym454$month(1L))
# Cyclical time
day_of_week(my_date)
# Durations
yearmonth(my_date) + months(0:2)
```

```{r mixtime-detach, include=FALSE, cache=FALSE}
# The rest of the course uses the tsibble time classes
detach("package:mixtime")
```

## What a `tsibble` checks {.code-small}

* Index + key must [uniquely identify]{.alert} each row: `as_tsibble()` errors on duplicates (find them with `duplicates()`)
* The [interval]{.alert} is shown in the header: `[1Y]`, `[1Q]`, `[1M]`, ...
* Missing time steps are [implicit gaps]{.alert}: find them with `has_gaps()`, make them explicit with `fill_gaps()`

```{r fill-gaps}
tsibble(year = c(2012, 2013, 2015, 2016), y = c(123, 39, 52, 110), index = year) |>
  fill_gaps()
```

# Example: Australian prison population

## Australian prison population

![](figs/Beechworth_prison.jpg){.photo}

## Read a csv file

Quarterly prisoner counts from the ABS, 2005 Q1 to 2016 Q4, by state, gender, legal status and indigenous status (ATSI: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander).

```{r prison}
prison <- readr::read_csv("data/prison_population.csv")
```
```{r prison2a, dependson="prison", echo=FALSE}
prison
```

## Convert to a time class

```{r prison3}
#| code-line-numbers: "2"
prison <- readr::read_csv("data/prison_population.csv") |>
  mutate(quarter = yearquarter(date))
```

```{r prison3a, dependson="prison3", echo=FALSE}
prison
```

## Remove the old date column

```{r prison4}
#| code-line-numbers: "3"
prison <- readr::read_csv("data/prison_population.csv") |>
  mutate(quarter = yearquarter(date)) |>
  select(-date)
```

```{r prison4a, dependson="prison4", echo=FALSE}
prison
```

## Declare the index and keys {.code-small}

```{r prison5}
#| code-line-numbers: "4-7"
prison <- readr::read_csv("data/prison_population.csv") |>
  mutate(quarter = yearquarter(date)) |>
  select(-date) |>
  as_tsibble(
    index = quarter,
    key = c(state, gender, legal, indigenous)
  )
```

```{r prison5a, dependson="prison5", echo=FALSE}
prison
```

# Example: Australian pharmaceutical sales

## Australian Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme

![](figs/pills.jpg){.photo}

## Australian Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme

::: {.block}
The [PBS]{.alert} is the Australian government drug subsidy scheme.
:::

::: {.fragment}
* Subsidises many pharmacy drugs
* Cost the government A$19.1 billion in 2024--25 (about 0.7% of GDP)
* Budget relies on forecasts of drug usage
:::

::: {.fragment}
`PBS` data: monthly, July 1991 to June 2008

* `Scripts` (prescriptions) and `Cost` (A$)
* By drug type (ATC2 x`r length(unique(PBS$ATC2))`), concession (x`r length(unique(PBS$Concession))`) and patient type (x`r length(unique(PBS$Type))`)
* ATC: Anatomical Therapeutic Chemical classification
:::

## Working with `tsibble` objects {.code-small}

```{r wide, include=FALSE}
options(width = 100)
```

```{r pbs1, dependson='wide'}
PBS
```

## `filter()`: choose rows {.code-small}

```{r pbs2}
PBS |>
  filter(ATC2 == "A10")
```

```{r medium, include=FALSE}
options(width = 78)
```

## `select()`: choose columns {.code-small}

```{r pbs3, dependson='medium'}
PBS |>
  filter(ATC2 == "A10") |>
  select(Month, Concession, Type, Cost)
```

## `summarise()`: combine over keys {.code-small}

```{r pbs4}
PBS |>
  filter(ATC2 == "A10") |>
  select(Month, Concession, Type, Cost) |>
  summarise(total_cost = sum(Cost))
```

## `mutate()`: create variables {.code-small}

```{r pbs5}
PBS |>
  filter(ATC2 == "A10") |>
  select(Month, Concession, Type, Cost) |>
  summarise(total_cost = sum(Cost)) |>
  mutate(cost_m = total_cost / 1e6)
```

`cost_m` is the total cost in A$ millions.

## Save the result {.code-small}

```{r pbs6}
a10 <- PBS |>
  filter(ATC2 == "A10") |>
  select(Month, Concession, Type, Cost) |>
  summarise(total_cost = sum(Cost)) |>
  mutate(cost_m = total_cost / 1e6)
```

```{r a10, echo=FALSE, dependson="pbs6"}
a10
```

```{r narrow, include=FALSE}
options(width = 60)
```

## Plot the result

```{r a10-plot, dependson="pbs6"}
autoplot(a10, cost_m) +
  labs(y = "A$ (millions)", title = "Australian antidiabetic drug sales")
```

## Hints

* `summarise()` always keeps the index
* Q1: `group_by(State)`, then `summarise()`
* Q2: `as_tibble()` first: it drops the tsibble structure, so `summarise()` no longer keeps the index
* Q3: `filter()`, then `summarise()`
:::

## Recap

* A tsibble has an **index**, **keys** and **measures**
* Index + keys uniquely identify each row
* The index needs a time class (`yearmonth()`, `as_date()`, ...)
* Use dplyr verbs to wrangle tsibbles
* `summarise()` combines over keys, keeping the index
